business_problem: Duke Energy needed to go beyond current US EPA regulations and replace slow physical inspection-based leak surveys with a rigorous end-to-end way to detect, monitor, and remediate methane emissions across its natural gas distribution assets.
solution_summary: Accenture, Avanade, and Microsoft helped Duke Energy build a first-of-its-kind, end-to-end Azure-based cloud platform for its natural gas distribution business. The implementation ingests satellite monitoring data and operating signals tied to pipelines, gas meters, and other assets, then uses analytics and artificial intelligence to quantify baseline methane emissions, prioritize likely leaks, and attach precise geolocation context for field response. The platform packages the resulting insights into graphic dashboards so leadership and operations teams can review findings at different levels of detail and coordinate remediation. Instead of relying only on physical inspections, Duke Energy now has a near real-time monitoring workflow that detects issues faster, improves repair prioritization, and provides a shared cloud foundation for wider asset and jurisdiction coverage as the program scales.
